name: Violet (Crayola)
lede: Violet (Crayola) is Crayola's own named shade of [[violet]], and our data finds it nearly identical to [[plum]].

sections.title: A crayon-box shade of violet
sections.body:
Wikipedia's Crayola color list is our only source for this name, crediting it to the Crayola line with no coining date given [1]. Our data finds it 2.8 units from [[plum]], close enough to read as almost the same color [2].

Further look-alikes are [[maximum-red-purple]] (4.3, redder), [[razzmic-berry]] (4.5, duller) and [[traffic-purple]] (4.6, more vivid) [2].

In LCH terms Violet (Crayola) measures lightness 40, chroma 49 and hue 337 degrees, a muted reddish purple rather than a pure spectral violet [2]. Crayola markets it alongside dozens of other named purples, and our sources give no account of why this particular shade earned the plain name "Violet" in that line [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3].
